extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and USPTO staff
extracted.subtask_short: handling patent fees and deposit accounts
extracted.subtask_description: Administrative rules and procedural requirements for payment, accounting, and submission of correspondence/records to the USPTO (fees, refunds, credit card use, deposit accounts, and small entity status). Covers how payments are to be made, itemized, applied, refunded, and how deposit-account authorizations operate.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.251 — reply with correspondence record or statement
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Office issues a notice under 37 CFR 1.251 (file unlocatable), the applicant or patentee must reply by providing a copy of (or producing) his or her record of all correspondence between the Office and the applicant/patentee for the application, patent, or other proceeding; if no such record exists, reply with a statement to that effect (37 CFR 1.251(a)(1)-(a)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If producing the record for copying under 1.251(a)(2), bring it to the Customer Service Center in the Office of Initial Patent Examination. The notice will include a PALM printout of contents entries. 37 CFR 1.251 generally applies where the entire file (not just certain documents) is unlocatable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time periods and consequences for reply to 37 CFR 1.251 notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Office will set a 3-month reply period in an application (extendable under 37 CFR 1.136(a) by three months up to 6 months); in a patent the Office will set a 6-month reply period (not extendable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to reply within 3 months in an application will result in abandonment of the application (37 CFR 1.251(b)). Failure to reply within three months can reduce patent term adjustment under 35 U.S.C. 154(b) by the number of days beyond the initial 3-month window. In patents, failure to comply may affect Office action under other rules (e.g., 37 CFR 41.128 or 10.18) and the only certified copy the Office can produce may be limited to the patent and application-as-filed, possibly harming enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office practice for missing documents vs. missing file
rubrics_metrics.description: When a document is missing from an application, Office practice is normally to call the applicant’s representative and request submission (generally by facsimile) of a copy rather than issue a 37 CFR 1.251 notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may issue a 1.251 notice to obtain a missing document if informal attempts fail. The 1.251 procedure is reserved generally for unlocatable files, not routine missing-document situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of appendices and information disclosure statements (IDS) in response to 1.251
rubrics_metrics.description: Any appendix or information disclosure statement submitted with an application is not in the Office’s PACR database; therefore the applicant/patentee must provide a copy of any appendix or IDS submitted with the application when replying to a 1.251 notice (with limited exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the Office can obtain copies of U.S. patent documents from internal databases, the Office is not requiring applicants/patentees to provide copies of U.S. patent application publications and patents that are among the record of correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.22 — fees payable in advance
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent fees and charges payable to the USPTO are required to be paid in advance at the time of requesting any Office action for which a fee is payable, except that under 1.53 applications may be accorded a filing date without payment of the basic filing fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should pay required fees when requesting fee-bearing actions to avoid processing issues or abandonment. See exceptions under 37 CFR 1.53.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.22(b) — fees must be itemized
rubrics_metrics.description: All fees paid to the USPTO must be itemized in each individual application, patent, or other proceeding so that it is clear for which purpose the fees are paid; the Office may return fees that are not itemized as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reference to 'filing fee(s)' is generally sufficient to cover filing/search/examination fees; references to 'any corresponding fee under 37 CFR 1.16' will cover surcharges, application size fee, excess claims fees, etc. Itemization is intended to help Office accounting and avoid returns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable non-credit methods of payment (37 CFR 1.23(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Payments must be in U.S. dollars and in the form of a cashier’s or certified check, Treasury note, national bank notes, or U.S. Postal Service money order. Checks/money orders must be payable to the Director of the USPTO (checks to Commissioner still accepted). Foreign payments must be immediately negotiable in the U.S.; mail-at-risk notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If payment is sent in other forms, the Office may delay or cancel credit until collection. Money sent by mail is at sender's risk; recommend registering letters containing money.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.23(b) — credit card payment acceptance and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Payments may also be made by credit card (except for replenishing deposit accounts). Payment must specify amount and necessary information; Office will not accept a general authorization to charge a card.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Credit Card Payment Form (PTO-2038) when possible. If credit card info is provided on forms other than the PTO form, the card number may become public record. The Office will not accept oral (telephonic) authorization to charge fees (except for information product/service fees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit card payment form (PTO-2038) and privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTO-2038 should be used for credit-card payment of patent or trademark process fees; the Office will not include the PTO-2038 among records open to public inspection in the file of a patent, trademark registration, or other proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customers are not required to use PTO-2038, but failure to use it risks making card information part of a publicly inspectable Office file if included elsewhere. If a card payment form lacks necessary info, a revised form must be submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet credit card payments — security code requirement (effective Jan 28, 2006)
rubrics_metrics.description: Credit card payment submissions made on the USPTO web site must include the card's 3- or 4-digit security code in addition to the card number; the security code is not required when submitting the paper PTO-2038 or other written authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Security code (CVV/CVV2/CVC2/CID) authenticates possession of the physical card. The online payment screen will include a mandatory field and info to locate the code. If you cannot read the code, contact the issuing financial institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit card facsimile payments and telephonic prohibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Credit card payments by facsimile are permitted except where facsimile submission is prohibited by 37 CFR 1.6(d); Office employees will not accept oral (telephonic) instructions to complete the Credit Card Payment Form or otherwise charge patent/trademark process fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure written authorization contains all necessary information; facsimile is acceptable in most circumstances, but oral authorizations are not accepted for charging process fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.26 — refunds of fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may refund any fee paid by mistake or in excess; a change of purpose after payment (e.g., withdrawing a filing) does not entitle the payer to a refund. The Office will not refund amounts of $25 or less unless specifically requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refunds will be by electronic funds transfer if banking info is provided, or by credit to the credit card account if the fee was paid by card. Requests for refund must generally be filed within two years of payment (not extendable), with special rules for deposit-account charge disputes. Certain reexamination refunds (specified amounts) will be by the form of original payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific reexamination refund amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Director decides not to institute reexamination: refund $1,690 for ex parte reexaminations (37 CFR 1.510) and $7,970 for inter partes reexaminations (37 CFR 1.913).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requester should indicate the form in which any refund should be made (e.g., check, EFT, credit to deposit account). Generally, reexamination refunds are issued in the form of the original payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office response when fee amount shown in notice was incorrect or fee increased
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Office has notified an applicant in writing that a fee is due and specified a dollar amount, timely submission of the specified amount should be considered compliance to avoid abandonment. If the payment is insufficient (incorrect amount or fee increased after mailing), the Office should notify applicant of insufficiency and give a new time period to submit the remaining balance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The written notification should state the reason for insufficiency (incorrect earlier amount or subsequent fee increase).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of insufficient payment — nonprovisional filing order
rubrics_metrics.description: If a payment submitted on filing of a nonprovisional application is insufficient and the applicant has not specified application of payment, the Office will apply the payment in this order until expended: (1) basic filing fee; (2) application size fee; (3) late filing surcharge; (4) processing fee for non-English application; (5) search fee; (6) examination fee; (7) excess claims fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should specify allocation to ensure intended fees are covered; otherwise Office follows this prescribed priority to determine which fees are satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of insufficient payment — provisional filing order
rubrics_metrics.description: If a payment submitted on filing of a provisional application is insufficient and the applicant has not specified allocation, the Office will apply the payment in this order until expended: (1) basic filing fee; (2) application size fee; (3) late filing surcharge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same practical guidance: specify allocations to avoid unexpected application of funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit accounts — establishment, minimums, and service charges (37 CFR 1.25(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposit accounts may be established upon payment of the establishment fee. A minimum deposit of $1,000 is required for general accounts; a minimum $300 for restricted subscription deposit accounts used exclusively for subscription order of patent copies. Monthly statements are rendered; remittance must be made promptly to restore the normal deposit value. Accounts with insufficient balance will not accept charges; service charges apply monthly if balance falls below required minimums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure sufficient funds are maintained to cover all fees/services requested. Each new account incurs a $10 opening charge (37 CFR 1.21(b)(1)); repeated suspensions for overdrafts may lead to account closure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charges that may be made to deposit accounts and authorization rules (37 CFR 1.25(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing, issue, appeal, international-type search report, international application processing, petition, and post-issuance fees may be charged to deposit accounts if sufficient funds exist. A general authorization to charge fees under 37 CFR 1.16–1.18 may be filed in an individual application for the pendency or a particular paper. An authorization to charge issue fee may be filed only after mailing of the notice of allowance (37 CFR 1.311(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A general authorization made prior to notice of allowance does not apply to issue fees. General authorizations do not apply to document supply fees (1.19), post-issuance fees (1.20), or miscellaneous fees (1.21), except to cover processing fees under 1.21(m) where a check or card payment is refused/charged back.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of 'filing fee' and 'basic filing fee' in deposit-account authorizations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will treat an authorization to charge 'the filing fee' as authorization to charge applicable fees under 37 CFR 1.16: basic filing, search, examination, excess claims, and application size fees. An authorization to charge 'the basic filing fee' will be treated as authorization to charge basic filing, search, and examination fees. Authorizations that exclude search/examination must specifically limit the authorization by reference to paragraphs of 1.16.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft authorizations precisely. Broad language will be interpreted to include 1.16 and 1.17 fees but not 1.19/1.20/1.21 unless explicitly stated as noted above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit-account authorizations — clarity and risks of ambiguity
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorizations to charge deposit accounts must be clear and unambiguous. Ambiguous or nonstandard authorizations risk being interpreted differently by the Office or causing fees to be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambiguous authorizations can lead to returned fees and require petitions or resubmissions, causing additional expense. Use standard/form language and consider submitting duplicate transmittal letters specifying the account to be charged to facilitate processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replenishment methods for deposit accounts (37 CFR 1.25(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposit accounts may be replenished by: (A) electronic funds transfer via Federal Reserve Fedwire (provide Treas NYC, routing code 021030004, USPTO Treasury account 13100001, and depositor's company name and account number); (B) EFT over the USPTO website; (C) mail via USPS to Director, USPTO, P.O. Box (provided); or (D) private delivery or hand-carry to Director, USPTO, Attn: Deposit Accounts, 2051 Jamieson Avenue, Suite 300, Alexandria, VA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using Fedwire, ensure due care in listing all account numbers to avoid processing delays. If a replenishment is refused (e.g., insufficient funds, stop payment), a processing fee under 37 CFR 1.21(m) will be charged to the deposit account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of overdrawn deposit accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: An overdrawn account will be immediately suspended and no charges accepted until balance is restored and a $10 payment (37 CFR 1.21(b)(1)) is made to cover Office work in suspending/reinstating the account and dealing with any interim charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authorization to charge basic filing/search/exam fees exists on an overdrawn account, a surcharge (37 CFR 1.16(f)) is required in addition to payment of the fees. Failure to timely pay filing fee and surcharge results in abandonment for affected applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit-account authorization for national-stage (35 U.S.C. 371) filings
rubrics_metrics.description: An authorization to charge fees under 37 CFR 1.16 in an application filed under 35 U.S.C. 371 will be treated as an authorization to charge fees under 37 CFR 1.492 (national stage fees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers for national stage entry that include authorization to charge 1.16 will be treated as authorization to charge 1.492 because timely payment of the national fee is necessary to avoid abandonment in the U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small entity fee reductions (35 U.S.C. 41(h)(1) and related rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees charged under 35 U.S.C. 41(a)/(b)/(d)(1) shall be reduced by 50% for any small business concern (as defined), independent inventor, or nonprofit organization (per 37 CFR 1.27), except where statute forbids. The Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2005 provides a 75% reduction of the filing fee under 35 U.S.C. 41(a)(1)(A) for a small entity filing electronically as prescribed by the Director (does not apply to design, plant, reissue, or provisional applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduced fees include filing/search/examination/application size/excess claims fees, extension of time, revival, appeal, issue fees, statutory disclaimer, and maintenance fees. Fees not reduced include certain petition/processing fees (other than revival), document supply fees, certificate of correction fees, reexamination request fees, miscellaneous fees, and international application fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and eligibility for small entity status (37 CFR 1.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: Small entity means a party who is a person (inventor/individual who has not assigned or is under no obligation to assign rights), a small business concern (meeting SBA size standards and not having assigned rights to a non-qualifying entity), or a nonprofit organization (university, 501(c)(3), nonprofit scientific/educational org, or qualifying foreign nonprofit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An inventor who has transferred some rights may still qualify if all parties who have rights also qualify. Licenses to a Federal agency from rights-determination under Executive Order 10096 or funding agreements under 35 U.S.C. 202(c)(4) generally do not disqualify. Security interests do not count as obligations to transfer rights unless defaulted upon.
